text_summary.body: A closing list numbers those Nebuchadnezzar carried away: 3,023 Jews in his seventh year, 832 persons from Jerusalem in his eighteenth, and 745 Jews taken by Nebuzaradan in his twenty-third — 4,600 persons in all.

setting.period: Nebuchadnezzar's 23rd year (582/581 BC on the Babylonian count)
setting.body: Josephus reports that in Nebuchadnezzar's twenty-third year, the fifth after the destruction, he campaigned in Coele-Syria against Ammon and Moab and then Egypt, and took Jews captive to Babylon. No Babylonian chronicle survives for these years.

constraints.subject: evt_01M4V7P26BWJJ0XTGZC1SCD4G0
constraints.textual_assertion: in the twenty-third year of Nebuchadnezzar
assumptions: Jer 52:28–30 counts Nebuchadnezzar's years Babylonian-style (its "seventh year" = the 597 capture, ABC 5); year 23 = Nisan 582 – Nisan 581 (Parker & Dubberstein).

constraints.subject: evt_01M4V7P26BWJJ0XTGZC1SCD4G0
constraints.textual_assertion: in the twenty-third year … carried away captive

competing_reconstructions.label: Jer 52:28–30 counts with an accession year
competing_reconstructions.summary: Its 7th and 18th years are Kings' 8th and 19th; the 23rd year is 582/581.

competing_reconstructions.label: The figures count adult males or a portion of the exiles
proponents: R. K. Harrison and C. L. Feinberg (via Guzik)
competing_reconstructions.summary: 3,023 may be a head count of deported adult males; the total of exiles was much higher (cf. 2 Kgs 24:14, 16).

commentary.paraphrase: Guzik, citing Harrison and Feinberg, takes the 4,600 as a partial count of adult males and accepts Cundall's accession-year explanation of the year numbers.

open_questions: Whether the 745 were taken from Judah or from Jews elsewhere (e.g. Egypt) is not stated.
